change: Nuclear preference now requires explicit avoided-emissions, avoided-harm, reliability and public-value accounting rather than preference language alone.
Clean-firm, fossil-displacement and reliability benefits must name and model a counterfactual resource or unserved-energy baseline.
Nuclear lifecycle GHG, land, material, water/thermal, safety and externality boundaries are explicit maturity gates.
The cube now rejects both anti-nuclear portfolio blind spots and pro-nuclear benefit overclaim through a comparative scorecard and exception ledger.
Fossil-displacement claims now require air-quality, public-health and beneficiary-distribution evidence where asserted.
